description: How the roles of the EV charging ecosystem relate to each other: who signs roaming agreements, who charges where, how sessions are paid and settled, and which data flows keep drivers and fleets informed.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Roaming agreements, subscriptions, and charging service contracts

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Day-to-day charging sessions, network operation, and depot charging

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Session payment and roaming settlement via CDRs

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Tariffs, availability, and cost and usage reporting

relations.name: Signs roaming agreements
relations.description: Negotiates roaming agreements with charge point operators, directly or via roaming hubs, so its drivers can charge across networks with one card or app.

relations.name: Publishes tariffs and live availability
relations.description: Exposes charge point locations, connector status, and tariff data over OCPI so the eMSP can show drivers accurate prices and availability before they plug in.

relations.name: Provides charging access and app
relations.description: Offers drivers a charge card and app subscription that bundles access to thousands of charge points across networks and borders into one account.

relations.name: Charges at public stations
relations.description: Plugs in at the operator's public and semi-public charge points, starting sessions via app, card, or ad-hoc payment and depending on the operator for uptime.

relations.name: Pays for charging sessions
relations.description: Pays the eMSP for consumed sessions through the app or charge card, expecting the price shown before charging to match the final invoice line.

relations.name: Settles roaming session charges
relations.description: Settles charge detail records for its drivers' roaming sessions with the operator, reconciling CDRs against agreed roaming tariffs each billing cycle.

relations.name: Contracts fleet charging services
relations.description: Contracts the eMSP for fleet charge cards, home reimbursement, and policy controls so company drivers can charge publicly under governed conditions.

relations.name: Reports fleet cost and usage
relations.description: Delivers consolidated charging cost, consumption, and CO2 reporting per vehicle and driver, feeding TCO tracking and ESG reports.

relations.name: Contracts depot and workplace charging
relations.description: Contracts the operator to install and run depot and workplace chargers, including load balancing so the site connection is not overloaded at shift changes.
